Subject: SLO scrub: p95/p99 latency expectations and next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we discussed for the SLO qualification:

Key targets you asked us to validate (end-to-end, client-observed):
- p95 <= 200 ms
- p99 <= 600 ms
- Sustained streaming sessions up to ~30s (average chunk interval 250ms) with up to 50 concurrent streams; burst capacity to 200 req/s for short windows
- Throughput baseline: 300 req/s peak during daytime traffic envelope; 1k req/s burst allowed for 5–10 minute windows

Immediate asks from Northbridge for PoC:
1) Test API key and a traffic/profile file (sample payloads, typical sequence lengths).
2) Procurement contact to coordinate PO/terms (for procurement/contract timeline).

What we’ll deliver for the 2-week PoC:
- Controlled traffic replay using your traffic_profile_v1.csv (please confirm)
- Server + client-side telemetry capturing e2e latency (client send to final token), server processing, queue time, and tail breakdowns
- A set of run variants: single-request, streaming (chunked), and burst profiles
- Weekly checkpoint + final readout with p95/p99 graphs, trace examples, and recommended config (batching, KV cache settings, quantization profile)

Attachments: traffic_profile_v1.csv (placeholder) — if you can share the actual CSV it’ll let us match load shape exactly.

Next step suggestions:
- Samantha: share a sanitized example payload set + procurement contact
- Rishi/Camila: propose PoC schedule and test config by Monday 7/14

I’ll loop in Laura for commercial alignment once we have the final traffic profile.

Cheers,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming Northbridge’s targets (end-to-end, client observed): p95 target of 180–200ms, p99 target of ~600ms (we understand p99 is harder). The product team will expect to see both raw numbers and the breakdown (client network + your runtime).

We can share a sanitized traffic_profile_v1.csv by EOD Monday (mixed small prompts ~50 tokens and larger LLM instructions ~600 tokens). Procurement looped in for PO — contact is Maria Ruiz (maria.ruiz@northbridge.ai).

A few clarifications from our side:
- Streaming behavior: chunks arrive every ~200–400ms; the UI keeps an open connection for up to 30s for long-running chains. We need to avoid stalls >500ms within a streaming session.
- Concurrency: typical active users ~50 concurrent streams, but we must support bursts to 200 requests/sec during peak marketing events for up to 8–10 minutes.
- Security: please confirm if we can sign an NDA and provide your SOC 2 summary before we exchange full production-like payloads. We attached our security questionnaire (northbridge_security_q_apr2025.pdf).

We’re good with a two-week PoC if Redwood can instrument client-side metrics and provide an on-call for the first 48 hours of the run.

Best,
Samantha

Subject: Re: SLO scrub: p95/p99 latency expectations and next steps

Looping internal team in with a proposed technical plan for the PoC — I’ll own the test orchestration workstream.

Proposed test matrix (initial):
- Profile A: baseline single-request (50–100 token prompts) at 300 req/s sustained for 10m; capture p50/p95/p99, server CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth
- Profile B: large requests (~600 tokens) at 40 req/s sustained; measure token generation time and end-to-end
- Profile C: streaming sessions (chunk interval 250ms) at 50 concurrent streams, 30s window; simulate burst to 200 req/s for 10m to validate fallbacks and routing

Config notes:
- Model: start with hosted gpt-like open variant (q4_8bit) to match throughput; record perf difference vs our float32 profile
- Batching: evaluate continuous batching windows of 5–10 ms and 20–50 ms to trade latency vs throughput
- KV cache warmup: run warmup with representative sessions to avoid cold-cache p99 spikes

Telemetry we will capture:
- Client send -> final token (e2e)
- Server ingress -> first byte / last token
- Queue time + batch size distribution
- GPU utilization, kernel stall events, and quantization fallback counters

Owner matrix:
- Camila: test harness + traffic replay (timeline: draft by Tuesday 7/15)
- Ben: streaming harness + alerting (on-call first 48h)
- Rishi: commercial/PO + customer comms
- Laura: pricing & escalation path if PoC shows significant infra delta

I’ll draft the mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf and drop a link to the runbook. Can someone confirm the test account credentials once we get the CSV from Samantha?

Thanks —
Camila
